issue.title: [202605] Bug: `crm/test_crm.py::test_acl_entry` fails with `Failed: "crm_stats_acl_entry_used" counter was not decremented or "crm_stats_acl_entry_available" counter was not incremented`

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Introduced in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/22166 many of the ports in the minigraph.xml output went from using the `alias` name to using the `non-alias` name but the associated testing code wasn't updated.
This failure is due to this.
```
{% if num_asics > 1 or hwsku_has_alias_name_collision %}
  {% set a_intf = intf_alias %}
{% else %}
  {% set a_intf = port_alias_map[intf_alias] %}
{% endif %}
{{- acl_intfs.append(a_intf) -}}
```
When you run `crm/test_crm.py::test_acl_entry` on a single-asic system on 202605 or later it will fail with:
```
E                         Failed: "crm_stats_acl_entry_used" counter was not decremented or "crm_stats_acl_entry_available" counter was not incremented
```
When reproducing we can see the test removes 2 ACL entries and expects the available ACL count to go from `2028` to
```
((Pdb)) p crm_stats_acl_entry_available
2034
```
But in reality it goes to `2038`
```
  Available Count
-----------------
             2038
```

The reason it calculates the available count wrong is it only considers the port-channels as acl binding points:
```
((Pdb)) p asicAclBindings
{'PortChannel104', 'PortChannel103', 'PortChannel101'}
```
So it thinks it should add `3 (ports) * 2 (acl rules) = 6` to the available count.

But in reality there are also 2 front panel ports bound to this ACL that aren't included in the `mg_facts['minigraph_acls']`:
```
Name        Type       Binding
----------  ---------  --------------
DATAACL     L3         Ethernet28
                       Ethernet88
                       PortChannel101
                       PortChannel103
                       PortChannel104
((Pdb)) mg_facts["minigraph_acls"]
{'DataAcl': ['Ethernet8', 'Ethernet36', 'Ethernet60', 'Ethernet64']}
```
If it did include the extra 2 non-portchannel ports it would've correctly calculated `5 (ports) * 2 (acl rules) = 10`

And the reason it only considers the port-channels as acl binding points is because the the `minigraph_facts.py` expects the `AttachTo` to contain alias ports not Ethernet ports:
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5ed0dc0820aab417d7986c603908533ff95ad789/ansible/library/minigraph_facts.py#L471-L480
```
                elif member in port_alias_to_name_map:
                    acl_intfs.append(port_alias_to_name_map[member])
```
```
((Pdb)) mg_facts['minigraph_port_alias_to_name_map']
{'Recirc0': 'Ethernet-Rec0', 'etp1': 'Ethernet0', ...
```
So because of https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/22166 we now see Ethernet ports in the AttachTo of the ACLs in minigraph:
```
<AttachTo>PortChannel101;PortChannel103;PortChannel104;Ethernet28;Ethernet88</AttachTo>
<InAcl>DataAcl</InAcl>
```

E.G 202511 looks like:
```
<AttachTo>PortChannel102;PortChannel104;PortChannel106;PortChannel108;PortChannel110;PortChannel112;PortChannel114;PortChannel116;PortChannel118;PortChannel120;PortChannel122;PortChannel124;PortChannel126;PortChannel128;PortChannel130;PortChannel132;PortChannel134;PortChannel136;PortChannel138;PortChannel140;PortChannel142;PortChannel144;PortChannel146;PortChannel148;PortChannel150;PortChannel152;PortChannel154;PortChannel156;PortChannel158;PortChannel160;PortChannel162;PortChannel164;etp17;etp18;etp19;etp20;etp21;etp22;etp23;etp24;etp25;etp26;etp27;etp28;etp29;etp30;etp31;etp32;etp33;etp34;etp35;etp36;etp37;etp38;etp39;etp40;etp41;etp42;etp43;etp44;etp45;etp46;etp47;etp48</AttachTo>
          <InAcl>DataAcl</InAcl>
```

### Steps to Reproduce

Run `crm/test_crm.py::test_acl_entry` on any single-asic SKU with non-portchannels on 202605 or later and it will fail.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

minigraph_facts.py and minigraph_dpg.j2 need to agree on the format they are using in the AttachTo output so we don't incorrectly miss the front panel ports.

resolution.title: mg_facts: Handle ACL bind points being non-alias
resolution.description:
### Description of PR
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/22166 made single-asic SKUs use non-alias ports as the bind points for ACLs.
The minigraph_facts.py was never updated to handle non-alias ports in the ACLs.

More details in https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/27215

Summary:
Fixes #27215

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

- [x] 202605
- [ ] N/A

### Test result
- 202605: internal image built on Aug 20th

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/22166 converted the ACL bindpoints to use non-alias ports.
We need to update minigraph_facts.py to handle non-alias ports otherwise `crm/test_crm.py::test_acl_entry` will fail

#### How did you do it?
Check if the port in the ACL `AttachTo` entry is in both `port_alias_to_name_map` and `port_name_to_alias_map`

#### How did you verify/test it?
Ran `crm/test_crm.py::test_acl_entry` and saw it passing on 202605 after the change

N/A
